items.title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Quality, Scale and Global Market Access to Drive India’s Industrial Transformation
items.summary: Addressing the Fourth National Conference on India’s Industrial Transformation, organised by the ISID and IDRA, Minister said that India must aim to become a globally recognised manufacturing nation. Shri Goyal identified quality, global market access, economies of scale and inclusivity as four key differentiators that could accelerate the transformation of India’s industrial landscape.

facts.text: The scale of India’s domestic market of 1.4 billion people, combined with access to international markets, could enable manufacturers to achieve affordability and competitive production costs.

Shri Goyal said that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 was a collective commitment of 1.4 billion Indians and called for coordinated efforts across government, industry, academia and research institutions to achieve this objective.

Recalling a conversation with the German Foreign Minister regarding the migration agreement between India and Germany and the requirement for 90,000 Indians annually, Shri Goyal said that he was told Germany needed substantially more Indian talent.

The Minister expressed confidence that India would continue to be the world’s fastest-growing major economy for another 20 to 25 years, attributing this prospect to the talent, skills and energy of its people.
